Status.note: The Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality issued an air construction permit for the Traceview Advanced Power Station on October 14, 2026, permit number 1720-00100 (https://opcgis.deq.state.ms.us/ensearchonline/get_doc.aspx?dt=finalp&id=1877274). The Permit Board agenda of October 13, 2026 lists the same permit (https://www.mdeq.ms.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Agenda-for-the-October-13-2026-PBM.pdf). A permit issued and land work under way fit pre-construction. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) lists the plant as under construction, less than 50 percent complete. I did not find a source that says physical construction has begun, so I used one step below that. Only the state permit and the EIA table support a change, so this is a single-step call.

Start year.note: Entergy's Traceview project page (https://www.entergymississippi.com/generation/traceview) gives an expected in-service date in 2029, and a Power Magazine article from October 2025 (https://www.powermag.com/entergy-mississippi-adding-third-gas-fired-power-plant-to-superpower-strategy/) says the same. Entergy's own filing at the Mississippi Public Service Commission, docket 2026-UA-55 from July 2026, gives August 2029. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) says 2028, so that source disagrees.

Turbine/Engine Technology.note: The air construction permit (https://opcgis.deq.state.ms.us/ensearchonline/get_doc.aspx?dt=finalp&id=1877274) describes a combustion turbine with duct burner, a heat recovery steam generator and a steam turbine. The public hearing notice from July 2026 (https://www.mdeq.ms.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Notice-of-Public-Hearing.pdf) calls it a 1x1 combined cycle plant.

Entergy says the site is north of West County Line Road between Livingston Road and the Natchez Trace Parkway (https://www.entergymississippi.com/generation/traceview), and the permit address is 1972 W County Line Road (https://opcgis.deq.state.ms.us/ensearchonline/get_doc.aspx?dt=finalp&id=1877274). The EIA point fits that description. GEM's current point is about 7.2 kilometers east.

Location accuracy.note: The satellite picture at the EIA point shows cleared and graded ground and a haul road, but no plant footprint such as stacks or a turbine hall. The date of the imagery is unknown. So the point is approximate.

location.review_note: The move is over 2 kilometers. The picture at the EIA point shows cleared ground but no plant footprint. The street address geocodes to the road edge at 32.40016, -90.20821, which is about 1.4 kilometers from the EIA point. A second look should check the 585 acre parcel north of West County Line Road.

qa.recommendation: Confirm that EIA plant 70187 is this plant and record its codes by hand. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists plant 70187, Traceview Advanced Power Station, in Madison County with generator CT1 (477.7 MW) and generator ST1 (341.7 MW), both natural gas combined cycle, planned for August 2028.
qa.note: The name, county, owner and permit all match this plant. GEM holds one combined cycle block as one unit, so the two EIA generators belong to Unit 1. Source: https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx

qa.recommendation: Decide which capacity to record. GEM has 760 MW. The EIA-860M table lists 819.4 MW nameplate (477.7 plus 341.7). Entergy's project page says 754 MW (https://www.entergymississippi.com/generation/traceview). The air permit lists 772,200 kW rated power (https://opcgis.deq.state.ms.us/ensearchonline/get_doc.aspx?dt=finalp&id=1877274) and the hearing notice says about 750 MW net (https://www.mdeq.ms.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Notice-of-Public-Hearing.pdf).
qa.note: The figures probably measure different things. EIA gives nameplate, which is the GEM measure. I did not change the value because no source states a nameplate that matches the others.

qa.recommendation: The announced step is dated April 2025. Entergy's news release of April 11, 2025 says the company selected a site on West County Line Road in Ridgeland and held a town hall about the plans (https://www.entergy.com/news/entergy-mississippi-selects-new-power-generation-site-prioritizes-community-needs). The Ridgeland city council approved the plans on April 24, 2025 according to a WLBT article already cited by GEM.
qa.note: I read the Entergy release. I did not re-open the WLBT article, so the second date rests on the title of the existing source.

qa.recommendation: Consider whether construction has started. The EIA table says under construction, but Entergy said site work would start in summer 2025 and construction in 2026 and I found no report that it began.
